items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes case against snake rescuer accused of capturing King Cobra
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed a criminal case against a snake rescuer accused of capturing and photographing a King Cobra. Justice Anant Ramanath Hegde on November 2 quashed the proceedings initiated against snake rescuer Dr. P Gowri Shankar. The Court held that the allegations did not establish that the petitioner had kept the snake in captivity, killed or injured it or uploaded its photographs on social media. “It is not the allegation that the petitioner has kept the king cobra in captivity, killed or injured [it], or uploaded the photograph,” the Court observed. items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday allowed devotees to offer prayers for Chhath Puja on private property, subject to strict supervision by the police and volunteers. [Kanchan Dubey and Ors v. The State of West Bengal and Ors] A Bench of Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge and Justice Om Narayan Rai was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by a group of women seeking permission to celebrate Chhath Puja for a few thousand devotees on a private property belonging to the Shib Krishna Debutter estate, located on the Ganga river bank at Rashbari ghat in Bally, Howrah. The Court framed several guidelines to monitor the crowd and enable the devotees to offer prayers. According to the plea, the High Court on several instances over the years had allowed the petitioners' community to conduct their rituals. The counsel for the petitioners submitted that the rituals would be completed within 19 hours.
